findings.issue_text: [BUG] `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` is not valid Java: `picocli` is a package name, not a class or variable, so this line does not compile. The quarkus runtime module fails to compile, breaking the entire build and every downstream artifact (CLI dist, operator image, tests). There is no static `exit(int)` on `picocli.CommandLine` either — the intended mechanism is `@Command(exitCodeOn...)` attributes or `CommandLine.execute()`'s return value, so even the intended behavior (setting a distinct process exit code) is unimplemented and `testFeatureNotEnabled` cannot assert an exit code of 4.

[BUG] The same invalid `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` call appears here, referencing the package `picocli` as if it were an invocable object. Compile error in the quarkus runtime module, identical build-breaking failure as in UpdateCompatibilityCheck; even if it compiled via some helper, no exit code of 4 would actually be returned to the shell since nothing wires this value to `System.exit`/`CommandLine.execute`.

[BUG] Changing RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 collides with the documented exit-code table in update-compatibility.adoc, which already assigns row `m|3` to 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The deployment must be shut down before applying the new configuration.' Any external automation (and the Operator itself, which consumes these exit codes to pick the update strategy) that branches on exit code 3 for the shutdown-required path now also sees code 3 for the generic recreate path, and consumers keyed on the old value 4 for recreate silently treat recreate results as feature-disabled; the docs table rows 2/3 are not updated in this diff, leaving the documented mapping wrong.

[ADVISORY] The custom image Dockerfile bakes `--features=rolling-updates` into the build, but the Operator's own default deployment mechanism (the StatefulSet pods the operator creates for Keycloak CRs without a FeatureSpec) has no corresponding enablement path shown in this diff, and the docs caution says the Operator 'will fail' when the feature is off. Any operator user upgrading an existing Keycloak CR that lacks `spec.features.enabled: [rolling-updates]` hits the documented hard failure with no migration path provided in the diff (no defaulting, no CRD conversion), so existing deployments break on operator upgrade until users hand-edit their CRs.

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently changed from 4 to 3, so any existing script/automation (or operator logic) that branches on the documented recreate exit code 4 now misclassifies a recreate-required result. A user with an existing upgrade script checking `exit code == 4` for recreate-required now sees code 3 fall through to an unhandled branch after upgrading Keycloak; the diff contains no test asserting exit code 3 for the incompatible/recreate path (testWrongVersions only asserts the error message, never the exit code), so this renumbering is unverified and undocumented as a breaking change.

[BUG] The new testFeatureNotEnabled test asserts only the error message and never asserts the FEATURE_DISABLED exit code (4), leaving the new exit-code contract path unverified. If picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) returns a wrong code (e.g. due to how picocli.exit is wired in a subcommand run()), the test still passes and CI scripts that gate on exit code 4 to distinguish 'feature disabled' from 'recreate required' get the wrong signal; this is exactly the new non-trivial behavior this diff introduces.

[ADVISORY] UpgradeTest is modified so that every deployment unconditionally enables the rolling-updates feature, and no test anywhere in the diff covers the operator's failure path when the feature is disabled, even though docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc promises 'Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail.' The documented disabled-feature failure behavior of the operator (what status condition/rollback the user sees when the feature is off but update.spec.strategy is set) has zero coverage; a regression that makes the operator silently proceed without the feature would not be caught, contradicting the caution box the same PR adds to the docs.

[ADVISORY] The docs exit-code table adds row 4 for 'feature rolling-updates is disabled' but the RECREATE row (3) previously documented as exit code 4 is renumbered without any note, so existing readers' saved runbooks referencing exit code 4 for recreate now resolve to the wrong condition. Operators following existing automation guides that interpret exit code 4 as 'recreate upgrade required' will, after this release, interpret a feature-disabled failure as a recreate-required result and shut down a deployment that merely needs --features=rolling-updates; the doc should call out the renumbering since exit codes are a public CLI contract.

[BUG] Changing RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and reassigning 4 to FEATURE_DISABLED silently breaks every existing consumer of the documented exit-code contract. Any CI script or operator automation written against the prior contract (exit 4 = recreate required) now interprets a feature-disabled failure as 'recreate upgrade required', or treats a genuine recreate-required result (now 3) as an unknown/zero-action status; the operator itself is the primary consumer of update-compatibility exit codes during upgrades, so a rolling-deploy orchestrator reading exit 4 will wrongly conclude a recreate is needed when the real cause is a disabled feature, masking the actual misconfiguration.

[BUG] The documentation asserts 'the Keycloak Operator will fail' when rolling-updates is not enabled, but this diff contains zero operator production-code changes implementing that failure, so the stated invariant is not enforced by anything traceable to this change. Operators following the new docs and enabling update strategies without the feature flag get a Keycloak CR that proceeds normally (the StatefulSet rolling update runs unconditionally as before), contradicting the documented behavior and defeating the entire purpose of gating rolling updates behind the preview feature — the only enforcement anywhere in the diff is on the two kc CLI commands, not on the operator path the doc governs.

[ADVISORY] The test change sets featureSpec.enabledFeatures unconditionally for every update-strategy test, so no test in the diff covers the newly documented operator failure mode when the feature is disabled. The docs added in this same diff promise the operator fails without the flag; since no test exercises a Keycloak CR with an update strategy but without rolling-updates enabled, a regression (or complete absence) of the operator-side gate ships undetected — whoever consumes the operator's rolling-update guarantees is bitten at upgrade time.

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changes from 4 to 3 and the value 4 is repurposed to mean FEATURE_DISABLED, with no versioning or migration path for existing automation consumers of the CLI contract. Any existing script/CI that already invokes `kc.sh update-compatibility check` (this command shipped before the flag) and branches on exit code 3 — which previously meant picocli usage error — now silently takes the 'recreate upgrade required' path, and any script branching on 4 as 'recreate required' now gets feature-disabled; the failure mode is scripts provisioning downtime or aborting on the wrong branch with no error surfaced. Exit codes are a public API contract for a shipped (preview) command and changing them in-place is an unversioned breaking change.

[ADVISORY] The feature gate for update-compatibility lives only in the CLI commands, while the docs claim the Keycloak Operator also fails without the feature, but no operator-side enforcement appears in this diff. If the operator's update-strategy path is not actually gated on the ROLLING_UPDATES feature (nothing in this diff wires Profile.isFeatureEnabled into operator reconciliation), the documented CAUTION in docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc ('Otherwise the Operator will fail') describes behavior that does not exist, and operators relying on the doc will get silent rolling behavior with the feature off. Verification requires the operator-side change; if it exists in a companion diff this drops to a doc/coordination nit.

[ADVISORY] The feature is enabled only in the test custom-image Dockerfile, so the flag's enablement story depends on the operator injecting --features=rolling-updates into the server build args, duplicating the feature list between the Keycloak CR FeatureSpec and the image build. The operator must now maintain the feature list in two places (FeatureSpec on the CR and whatever it bakes into kc.sh build); a user enabling rolling-updates via FeatureSpec on a prebuilt image that was built without the flag gets a server where Profile.isFeatureEnabled is false and update-compatibility exits 4, which is confusing to diagnose since the CR says the feature is on. This is the classic client+server parallel-configuration drift pattern with no single source of truth.

[BUG] The documented public exit code contract is silently renumbered: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changes from 4 to 3 and exit code 4 is repurposed to mean FEATURE_DISABLED, with no versioning, deprecation, or flag preserving old semantics. Any existing automation (CI pipelines, operator-side scripts, customer tooling) that already invokes `kc.sh update-compatibility` and branches on exit code 4 == 'recreate required' will now interpret a recreate-required result (exit 3) as success/fall-through, and will interpret a feature-disabled failure (exit 4) as 'recreate required' — silently wrong upgrade decisions during rolling deploys; this repurposing of a previously shipped public contract is done in-code without any documented migration path or human-acknowledged acceptance of the break.

[ADVISORY] The new testFeatureNotEnabled test runs both subcommands in a single @Launch and asserts only the error message, with no assertion that picocli exits with CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4) rather than a generic usage/software error. If the FEATURE_DISABLED exit code regresses to a generic picocli error code (1 or 2), the operator's documented 'code 4 means feature disabled' contract silently breaks while the test still passes, leaving the operator unable to distinguish 'user must enable the feature' from a real software failure; the exit-code contract introduced in this diff has no negative-path coverage.

[ADVISORY] The doc template hard-codes `--features=rolling-updates` into the example command, baking the preview-stage workaround into the rendered command itself rather than presenting it as a preview-only prerequisite. When the feature graduates from preview and the flag becomes a no-op or is removed, the rendered docs will instruct users to pass a stale/removed feature argument; also during preview, users copying the command get the feature enabled without reading the CAUTION box, contradicting the guide's intent that the flag is an explicit opt-in.

[BUG] testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message and never the new FEATURE_DISABLED exit code, so a regression that prints the error but exits 0 (or any other code) passes the test. The entire new behavior of CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (=4) — the exit-code contract that scripts and the operator's container invocation rely on to distinguish 'feature disabled' from 'recreate required' (=3) — is unverified; a bug swapping or breaking the exit code in UpdateCompatibilityCheck/UpdateCompatibilityMetadata ships undetected. Checked UpdateCommandDistTest.java in this diff: no assertEquals(4, ...) anywhere for the disabled-feature path.

[ADVISORY] testMissingOptionOnSave uses assertNoMessage("Missing required argument") instead of asserting the actual success/preview-warning behavior now that ENABLE_FEATURE is passed, so it verifies absence of an error string rather than the feature-enabled happy path it was converted into. The metadata-save path with the feature enabled is only proven by testCompatible later; this test contributes false confidence — it passes even if the metadata subcommand silently does nothing after the feature gate. Checked UpdateCommandDistTest.java in this diff: no positive assertion (message or exit code) in this test.

[ADVISORY] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 and the new FEATURE_DISABLED took 4, but no test in this diff asserts either the new recreate exit code (3) or FEATURE_DISABLED (4), leaving the documented exit-code table (update-compatibility.adoc rows 3 and 4) verified only by documentation. Any consumer (operator upgrade logic, CI scripts) branching on the old value 4 for 'recreate required' now silently misreads it as 'feature disabled'; a test asserting the exact exit codes would have pinned the contract. Checked UpdateCommandDistTest.java and UpgradeTest.java in this diff: only exit code 0 is asserted (testCompatible line ~74).

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from 4 to 3 in the same release that introduces a new exit code 4, silently redefining the wire contract of `kc.sh update-compatibility check` consumed by the Operator during rolling upgrades. Any operator or automation (including the operator's upgrade logic that drives UpdateStrategy and any out-of-tree scripts) written against the documented contract where exit code 4 means 'recreate upgrade required' now receives 3 — which picocli documents as an error class — so during a mixed-version rolling deploy an old operator pod evaluating a new-version server pod will misclassify 'recreate required' as a usage/software error and fail the upgrade loop instead of falling back to Recreate; nothing in this diff updates the operator's exit-code interpretation to the new values, and this cannot be disabled without a code deploy.

[ADVISORY] The operator's custom test image bakes the preview feature `rolling-updates` into the container build unconditionally via --features=rolling-updates, coupling the feature default to the image rather than to the Keycloak CR spec. Operators who reuse this Dockerfile pattern get a preview feature enabled as a build-time default, so disabling it per-deployment via spec.features becomes impossible without rebuilding the image, and behavior diverges between the stock image (feature off) and custom images (feature on) for the same spec — this diff also moves feature enablement from UnsupportedSpec to FeatureSpec only in the test, so any real cluster reconciler relying on the old `unsupported` field path is left with no writer for the feature.

[ADVISORY] Reassigning the meaning of exit code 4 (from RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE to FEATURE_DISABLED) silently changes the contract for every existing automation that invokes `kc.sh update-compatibility check`. Any deployment script, CI pipeline, or older Operator version in a mixed cluster that already branches on exit code 4 (documented until now as 'recreate upgrade required, shut down before applying') will, after upgrading Keycloak, interpret a disabled-feature condition as the recreate-required path and proceed to shut down the deployment unnecessarily — or, worse, a recreate-required result now exits 3, which existing consumers treat as an unknown/unhandled code and take no action while reporting success. There is no deprecation window or compat mapping in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The documented public exit code contract is silently renumbered: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changes from 4 to 3 and exit code 4 is repurposed to mean FEATURE_DISABLED, with no versioning, deprecation, or flag preserving old semantics. Any existing automation (CI pipelines, operator-side scripts, customer tooling) that already invokes `kc.sh update-compatibility` and branches on exit code 4 == 'recreate required' will now interpret a recreate-required result (exit 3) as success/fall-through, and will interpret a feature-disabled failure (exit 4) as 'recreate required' — silently wrong upgrade decisions during rolling deploys; this repurposing of a previously shipped public contract is done in-code without any documented migration path or human-acknowledged acceptance of the break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new testFeatureNotEnabled test runs both subcommands in a single @Launch and asserts only the error message, with no assertion that picocli exits with CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4) rather than a generic usage/software error. If the FEATURE_DISABLED exit code regresses to a generic picocli error code (1 or 2), the operator's documented 'code 4 means feature disabled' contract silently breaks while the test still passes, leaving the operator unable to distinguish 'user must enable the feature' from a real software failure; the exit-code contract introduced in this diff has no negative-path coverage.

adjudication.rationale: In `UpdateCommandDistTest#testFeatureNotEnabled`, the new test launches `UpdateCompatibility` + `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata` and only asserts the error text, without asserting the process exit code. The diff introduces a new explicit exit-code contract (`CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`) and both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck#run` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata#run` call `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` when `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` is disabled, but there is no negative-path test asserting that `4` is actually returned (so a regression to Picocli’s generic exit codes could go unnoticed). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a functional defect in the implementation shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from 4 to 3 in the same release that introduces a new exit code 4, silently redefining the wire contract of `kc.sh update-compatibility check` consumed by the Operator during rolling upgrades. Any operator or automation (including the operator's upgrade logic that drives UpdateStrategy and any out-of-tree scripts) written against the documented contract where exit code 4 means 'recreate upgrade required' now receives 3 — which picocli documents as an error class — so during a mixed-version rolling deploy an old operator pod evaluating a new-version server pod will misclassify 'recreate required' as a usage/software error and fail the upgrade loop instead of falling back to Recreate; nothing in this diff updates the operator's exit-code interpretation to the new values, and this cannot be disabled without a code deploy.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the CLI contract in `CompatibilityResult`: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` is changed from 4 to 3 while a new `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` is introduced. This is a real behavioral change for any consumer relying on the previous exit code mapping, and the diff does not show any compatibility shim (e.g., still returning 4 for recreate) or coordinated update of external consumers. While the finding’s specific claims about the Operator’s exact interpretation aren’t verifiable from this diff, the exit-code remapping itself is directly evidenced and can break existing automation/scripts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The operator's custom test image bakes the preview feature `rolling-updates` into the container build unconditionally via --features=rolling-updates, coupling the feature default to the image rather than to the Keycloak CR spec. Operators who reuse this Dockerfile pattern get a preview feature enabled as a build-time default, so disabling it per-deployment via spec.features becomes impossible without rebuilding the image, and behavior diverges between the stock image (feature off) and custom images (feature on) for the same spec — this diff also moves feature enablement from UnsupportedSpec to FeatureSpec only in the test, so any real cluster reconciler relying on the old `unsupported` field path is left with no writer for the feature.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does unconditionally add `--features=rolling-updates` to `operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image` (`RUN ... kc.sh build ... --features=rolling-updates`), which will make custom images built from this recipe differ from the stock image in terms of feature enablement. That is a concrete, diff-grounded coupling concern. However, the finding’s stronger claims (e.g., that disabling via `spec.features` becomes impossible without rebuilding, and that a real reconciler is left with no writer because only the test moved from `UnsupportedSpec` to `FeatureSpec`) are not verifiable from this diff alone, since no operator reconciliation logic is shown and the runtime vs build-time override behavior isn’t demonstrated here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Reassigning the meaning of exit code 4 (from RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE to FEATURE_DISABLED) silently changes the contract for every existing automation that invokes `kc.sh update-compatibility check`. Any deployment script, CI pipeline, or older Operator version in a mixed cluster that already branches on exit code 4 (documented until now as 'recreate upgrade required, shut down before applying') will, after upgrading Keycloak, interpret a disabled-feature condition as the recreate-required path and proceed to shut down the deployment unnecessarily — or, worse, a recreate-required result now exits 3, which existing consumers treat as an unknown/unhandled code and take no action while reporting success. There is no deprecation window or compat mapping in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes the numeric contract of CLI exit codes: `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` is changed from 4 to 3 and a new `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` is introduced. Both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata` now exit with `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` when `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` is not enabled. This is a backwards-incompatible behavior change for any existing automation that interpreted exit code 4 as “recreate required”, and the diff does not show any compatibility shim/mapping (it just changes constants and behavior). This is a concrete, diff-grounded compatibility concern rather than an internal correctness bug.
